maps.title: Map of the Indian tribes of North America, about 1600 A.D. along the Atlantic, & about 1800 A.D. westwardly
maps.creator: Albert Gallatin; American Antiquarian Society
maps.credit: Albert Gallatin; Pendleton’s Lithography. David Rumsey Historical Map Collection, list no.3388.001. Digital image © Cartography Associates.

rights.statement: CC BY-NC-SA 2.0. Noncommercial reuse with attribution and share-alike terms.

maps.annotation: Gallatin assembled this map for an American Antiquarian Society publication in 1836. Its title distinguishes eastern depictions around 1600 from western depictions around 1800. Compare its historical naming and classifications with later maps; its labels do not define current communities or borders.

maps.title: Catawba deerskin map: archival reproduction
maps.historicalTitle: [Map of the several nations of Indians to the Northwest of South Carolina]
maps.creator: Unidentified Indigenous maker; colonial copy associated with Francis Nicholson
maps.dateNote: LOC's guide distinguishes presentation around 1721 from its 1929 color photostat, catalogued under a 1724 call number. The supplied image should therefore not be described as an intact original 1721 deerskin or as made in 1929 without identifying its reproduction.
maps.credit: Underlying mapmaker and colonial copyist unnamed. Supplied digital reproduction; exact scan provenance unconfirmed. Historical interpretation: Library of Congress and Newberry Library.

rights.statement: Underlying historical cartography is public domain. The saved LOC record permits reuse subject to item advisories; it describes a 1929 photostat. Exact scan provenance of this owner-supplied reproduction remains unconfirmed; do not attribute its digitization to LOC.

maps.annotation: An archival reproduction preserves a copied network of communities and paths drawn from Indigenous knowledge. The conventional Catawba title does not establish the maker’s identity. Colonial annotations and multiple copying stages make its production history essential context for interpretation.

preview.alt: Supplied digital reproduction of the Catawba map, with circles for historical communities and connecting paths; copying and scan identification are explained in the record.
preview.changes: Original owner-supplied pixels retained. The map-room and profile images display the whole frame; homepage backgrounds use CSS cropping and overlays. No generated content.

inspection.scope: Actual owner-supplied digital reproduction visually inspected. LOC guide and saved full indexed item text read; direct item access remains blocked. Creator, surviving-copy dates and rights follow the identified archive record, with stated uncertainty. rights.statement: The item-specific page leaves copyright status undetermined and permits links. Do not embed this copy.

maps.annotation: Powell grouped North American Indigenous languages into the linguistic stocks used by nineteenth-century federal ethnology. maps.credit: A new map of the Cherokee Nation, 1760, hmap1760k5, Hargrett Rare Book and Manuscript Library, University of Georgia Libraries; presented by the Digital Library of Georgia. Engraved by Thomas Kitchin.
maps.annotation: Kitchin’s 1760 engraving names Cherokee towns and rivers. Its margin credits an unidentified Indigenous draught, mediated through a London magazine publication. Compare this historical representation with Cherokee accounts; it does not establish present government boundaries.
maps.perspective: Colonial engraving / mediated Indigenous geographic knowledge

inspection.scope: Read the complete actual archive record and manifest. Inspected the complete downloaded 3065x2372 scan at original resolution, including the cartouche, town/river labels and bottom engraver/source credit.
inspection.observedFeatures: Landscape sheet; named towns along rivers; mountain symbols; scale; decorated lower-left title; source/engraver credit below the map.
inspection.limits: No georeferencing, modern town equivalence, boundary inference or identification of the unnamed draught maker.

maps.annotation: Attributed to Greenleaf Dearborn, this 1837–1838 manuscript depicts military forts and routes around the Okefenokee during the Second Seminole War. It records an Army viewpoint, rather than Seminole territorial authority or present boundaries.

inspection.limits: No full handwriting transcription, exact sensitive-place coordinates, present boundaries or certainty beyond the archive's author attribution.
